0b88f124469ddefbc556439157e46dbe7c90600b.why: selected facts provide evidence for Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma

ranked_facts.why: specific immunophenotypic markers consistent with lymphoma
presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid

fact_rationales.F10: Brain biopsy showing CD5− CD10− CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER− is diagnostic for Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.
fact_rationales.F13: Presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid is highly suggestive of Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.
fact_rationales.F7: Hyperintensities on T2-weighted FLAIR MRI are seen in multiple conditions, including Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma and Multiple Sclerosis, but are less specific for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy.
fact_rationales.F8: Absence of contrast enhancement on T1-weighted FLAIR MRI with contrast is not typical for Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma, which often shows enhancement.

why.FLAT.2: The champion FLAT.2, Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma, is the best explanation for the observed case due to the presence of lymphoma cells in the cerebrospinal fluid, brain biopsy results showing CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER−, and imaging findings of hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles on T2-weighted FLAIR MRI, which are consistent with the diagnosis of Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma.
